meta.tagline: Handball apparel, made in Canada's smallest sport
meta.description: Apparel for Canadian handball. There are a few thousand of us and not one shop that sells anything with the sport's name on it — so we made one.

home.heroTitle: Handball barely exists here. Wear it anyway.
home.heroBody: There are a few thousand of us in this country. No aisle in any store, no kit in any window, nothing at the mall with the word on it. Every other sport gets to be worn. This one doesn't. So we made the thing that should already exist.
home.gapTitle: A sport you can't buy into
home.gapBody: Walk into any sporting goods store in Canada and you will find hockey, basketball, soccer, running, and a wall of gym wear. You will not find handball. Not a shirt, not a hoodie, not a sticker. The sport is played in this country — in school gyms, on beaches, at clubs holding on with volunteers — and none of it is visible. That's the whole reason this exists.

fund.title: 10% back into Canadian handball
fund.basisMerch: 10% of gross revenue from every order placed here.
fund.basisAll: 10% of gross revenue across everything we sell.
fund.whyBody: Handball in Canada does not lose players because the sport is hard to like. It loses them because a club can't find a goal to buy, a school can't source twelve size-2 balls, and a beach programme can't get boundary lines across the border. Money is the bottleneck at exactly the moment a programme is most fragile — and a shirt is a strange but honest way to move some.
fund.howBody: Equipment grants to clubs, schools and beach programmes — the goals, balls and nets they otherwise go without. Applications open once the first drop sells through.
fund.transparencyBody: We publish what came in, what went out and who received it, every quarter, on this page. A donation promise you can't audit is just marketing.
